description: Team Orbital is a team at the Dubai UAE local event, working remotely. We are making a static comparison tool for three lunar south pole sites: Malapert A rim, Nobile Crater west rim and Amundsen rim. It shows Sun and Earth elevation against the horizon, time to sunset and Earthset, and sunlight and Earth-visibility windows. Geometry only, precomputed from JPL ephemerides. AI tools were used and are disclosed.
summary: Lunar South Pole Site Comparison is a web page that compares three lunar south pole sites: Malapert A rim, Nobile Crater W rim, and a site near Amundsen crater. Using NASA JPL SPICE ephemeris data and terrain horizons built from LRO LOLA elevation data, it shows when the Sun and Earth are above each site's local horizon over a date range you choose. For each site it reports the Sun-visible and Earth-in-view percentages, the longest dark and Earth-out periods, and the next sunset and Earthset. You set four thresholds, the page marks each one PASS or FAIL, gives an overall result, and ranks the sites. A horizon margin slider and a sweep chart show how sensitive the results are. The calculations run in the browser in C++ compiled to WebAssembly. The data covers one year of hourly samples from 2026-11-15. This is a geometry-only comparison with no power, thermal or antenna model, so it does not recommend a landing site. Site coordinates are user-reported and unverified. Most of the code was written with AI chat assistants (Claude and ChatGPT); see the limits page on the live site.
details: A web page comparing three lunar south pole sites. It shows when the Sun and Earth clear each site's terrain horizon over one year, checks four user thresholds with PASS or FAIL, and ranks the sites. Calculations run in C++ compiled to WebAssembly.
dataRefs: LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) data, NASA PDS Geosciences Node
NASA JPL NAIF SPICE: de440s.bsp (planetary ephemeris)
NASA JPL NAIF SPICE: naif0012.tls (leap seconds)
NASA JPL NAIF SPICE: moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc (lunar orientation)
NASA JPL NAIF SPICE: moon_de440_250416.tf (lunar frame kernel)
projectRefs: LOLA LDEM_75S_120M terrain file, downloaded from the MIT Imbrium mirror
